title: Annotatio III §.V: Paschasius (IX) vs Bertram — conversion asserts; Otrokocsi on crassior substantial sense
pass_a_gloss: Until at last in the ninth Century there arose Paschasius Radbertus, remembered in the preceding annotation, about to oppose Bertram, who with the Ancients contended that the Eucharistic bread is also a Figure of Christ’s body, and contending with assertions of this sort which expressly professed a Conversion of bread into Christ’s body: e.g. when he said: Under the visible species of bread nothing other than Christ’s flesh is offered. Likewise: Bread is converted into flesh, and wine into blood. Lib. de corpore & sang. Domini, ch. 10 & 20, alleged by Francis Foris Otrokocsi in the Irenicum ch. 6 §. 1 p. 69, and commenting on Paschasius’s latter proposition thus: Namely of a somewhat crasser and substantial conversion, in Paschasius’s mind, otherwise than some of the ancients and Bertram himself spoke of sacramental and mystic speech and immutation.
pass_b_english: Ninth century: Paschasius Radbertus rises against Bertram (who with the Ancients kept the bread a Figure) and expressly professes conversion — under visible bread-species only Christ’s flesh is offered; bread into flesh, wine into blood (De corp. & sang. Dom. 10 & 20).
Otrokocsi: Paschasius means a crasser substantial conversion, unlike ancients/Bertram’s sacramental-mystic speech.
source_text: Usque dum Seculo demum IX. exurgeret præced. annot. memoratus Paschasius Rhadebertus, Bertramum, panem Eucharisticum cum Veteribus, etiam Figuram corporis Christi contendentem, oppugnaturus, assertis autem hujusmodi, decertans, quæ Conversionem panis in corpus Christi, disertè profitebantur: e.g. cùm diceret: Sub specie panis visibilis, nihil aliud quam caro Christi porrigitur. Item: Panis in carnem, & vinum in sanguinem convertitur. lib. de corpore & sang. domini, cap. 10. & 20., allegante Francisco Foris Otrokocsi in Irenico cap. 6. §. 1. p. m. 69. ac sequenti modô in posteriorem Paschasii propositionem commentante: Scil. de crassiusculâ & substantiali conversione, ex mente Paschasii, secus quam aliqui veterum atque etiam ipse Bertramus, de sacramenti & mystica locutione & immutatione, locuti sunt nonnulli.
